items.title: Lester Santiago Interview, 1959-01-09
items.q: And at that time, John Brunus, that was one of his first jobs that he had on the ship. He was a young boy right out of college. And Harold Dajon would teach both of us.

ctx.x: From New Orleans to New York City. And while traveling on a ship, they decided that the band would have to play to entertain the passengers. And those people had their own music. So they presented me the music on one trip, and I told them I didn't know how to read. So they got someone from off the ship, a passenger, to play my part. So Harold told me, he said, well, Leslie said you're a fine piano player, but they're going to have to leave you go, he said, because you don't read. He said, I've been behind you to…
Yeah, I worked with Larry too.

items.title: John "Picky" Brunious Interview, 1959-05-26
items.q: Lester told us a little bit about him. Lester, that's right.

ctx.x: That's right. Mr. and Mrs. Martinez used to own a doghouse. Big fat woman, great big woman. And the man was a little bit of skinny man like that, man. Boy, that was a combination. And both of them used to get drunk. Boy, I didn't raise them saying anything. They raised more than the customers raised. Well, in that band, in that band, uh, I was playing trumpet. My brother-in-law, Eddie Johnson, was playing saxophone. My brother-in-law, Boynel Santiago. Did y'all know about Boynel? Oh, yeah. We know about him.
Lester told us a little bit about him. Lester, that's right.
